inputs.name: zones
inputs.description: Zones BIND serves, by name, such as { "example.com" = { type = "primary", records = [...] } }. A primary holds records; a secondary copies the zone from its primaries.

inputs.name: tsig_keys
inputs.description: TSIG keys for zone transfers, by name, with each key's base64 secret, as tsig-keygen prints it. They use hmac-sha256. The config is written with content_wo when any are set, so the secrets stay out of state and the plan.

inputs.name: soa
inputs.type:
object({
    mname   = optional(string)
    rname   = optional(string, "hostmaster")
    refresh = optional(number, 3600)
    retry   = optional(number, 900)
    expire  = optional(number, 1209600)
    minimum = optional(number, 300)
  })
inputs.description: SOA fields for primary zones. mname defaults to the zone's first NS record at the apex. rname is the contact's mailbox with the @ as a dot, such as "hostmaster.example.com.", or a name relative to the zone. The serial is set on the host.

inputs.name: default_ttl
inputs.description: TTL, in seconds, for records that don't give their own.

inputs.name: listen_on
inputs.description: Addresses BIND answers on, port 53. "any" means every IPv4 and IPv6 address.

inputs.name: recursion
inputs.description: Answer recursive queries too, for localhost and the host's own networks only. Off, BIND answers only for its own zones and refuses everything else. For a resolver, circuit-unbound is the better fit.
